question: What is the fewest given numbers a Sudoku can start with and still have exactly one solution?
answer: 17. Gary McGuire's team proved in 2012, by an exhaustive computer search, that no 16-clue puzzle has a unique solution. Collectors had already gathered tens of thousands of 17-clue puzzles but never one with 16. Proving that something never exists took checking every case.
move: Showing something never happens can take far more work than one example.
ask: Which never have I stated that I have not actually checked?
trap: Guessing far fewer, since a clever puzzle seems to need little.
source: McGuire, Tugemann and Civario, There is no 16-clue Sudoku, 2012
